node-1.label: Right scrotum is swollen and rapidly growing without local pain

node-2.label: A 50-year-old Japanese man, non-smoker, with hypertension treated with ARB daily and no known allergies

node-4.label: A puncture at a prior hospital yielded red-colored fluid

node-5.label: No history of trauma or infections including STDs; physical examination revealed swelling on the right side

why.why: Ultrasound and MRI show a multilocular cystic lesion with septa but no solid component or enhancing rim, and contents consistent with hematoma; pathology shows bland tall columnar cells with no stromal invasion or papillary growth, and IHC (EpCAM+, BerEP4+, WT-1+, ER+, PR+, calretinin-, D2-40-) supports a benign epithelial cyst. These imaging and pathological findings effectively exclude scrotal/testicular malignancy, so confidence is reduced from 0.6 to 0.05.

Imaging demonstrates a multilocular cystic lesion with contents consistent with hematoma, and the red aspirate likely reflects prior hemorrhage. Although the absence of trauma was initially concerning, the imaging features and expert interpretation support a benign hematocele/cystic hematoma, raising confidence from 0.2 to 0.45.

There is no history of trauma, STD, or infection, the aspirate is bloody rather than inflammatory, and imaging/pathology show no inflammatory or infectious features; expert analyses do not support an infectious/inflammatory cause. Confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.01.

Imaging showing a multilocular cystic lesion without a solid component and pathology confirming a bland benign epithelial lining support a benign cystic collection; the red aspirate is explained by prior hemorrhage rather than a simple clear hydrocele. This raises confidence from 0.15 to 0.35, though the more specific benign epithelial cyst is favored.

node-10.label: Ultrasound and MRI show multilocular cystic lesion with septa, no solid component or enhancing rim, contents consistent with hematoma

node-11.label: Ultrasound shows multilocular cyst attached to testis with no testicular abnormalities

node-12.label: Pathology shows bland tall columnar cells lining the cyst with no stromal invasion or papillary growth

node-13.label: Immunohistochemistry: EpCAM+, BerEP4+, WT-1+, ER+, PR+, calretinin-, D2-40-

node-14.label: Red aspirate likely reflects prior hemorrhage within the cyst

node-15.label: Benign epithelial cyst of the testicular adnexa (e.g., mesothelial/epididymal cyst)

attrs.why: Imaging shows a multilocular cystic lesion without a solid component, pathology reveals bland tall columnar cells without stromal invasion or papillary growth, and IHC (EpCAM+, BerEP4+, WT-1+, ER+, PR+, calretinin-, D2-40-) supports a benign epithelial cyst rather than malignant mesothelioma or testicular cancer. The red aspirate is explained by prior hemorrhage, making a benign epithelial cyst of the testicular adnexa the most likely diagnosis.
